prompt: Increasingly, people pay a monthly subscription to use products such as software, cars, furniture and even clothing, instead of buying them outright. Do you think this is a positive or a negative development?
essay:
Paying monthly for access to a product, rather than buying it once, has spread from software to cars, furniture and even children's clothing. On the whole I regard this as a negative development, although there are cases where a subscription is genuinely the better arrangement.

The strongest argument in its favour is that some products are not really finished when they are sold. Software needs regular security updates, and a car needs servicing and eventually replacing; a subscription that bundles these costs into a predictable monthly payment spares the customer an unexpected bill. Subscriptions also lower the barrier to entry, since a household can use an expensive appliance without having the savings to buy it, and they suit people who need something only for a limited period, such as parents of a baby who will outgrow its cot within a year.

The problems begin when the model is applied to products that need no ongoing support. A sofa or a dining table does not change after delivery, yet a subscription turns it into a payment that never ends, and over its lifetime the customer usually pays far more than the purchase price. More seriously, the balance of power shifts to the company. It can raise the price, remove features or change the terms, and the customer's only option is to cancel and lose access to something they may have paid for several times over. Many services also rely on people forgetting what they have signed up to, and makes cancellation deliberately awkward.

For these reasons I believe the trend is more harmful than helpful. Subscriptions make sense for products that require continuous service, but for most physical goods they are simply a more expensive and less secure way of owning nothing. Consumers would benefit from rules requiring that cancelling be as easy as signing up.
title: Paying monthly instead of owning
